correctness.rationale: All 24 vertices have unit norm. Every distinct Gram value is minus one, minus a half, zero, or plus a half, with 96 plus-half unordered pairs (verified both analytically by vertex types and by an exact-rational checker). For thresholds s>=sqrt(2/3), intersections can occur only between these 96 pairs; triple-intersections have zero measure since 3s<=sqrt6. Standard S3 one-coordinate marginal integrates to P(s), while the orthogonal two-coordinate marginal is exactly uniform on a disk, yielding Q(s) by direct area integration. The pair-cap quadratic onset Q(sqrt3/2-delta)=4 delta^2/(pi sqrt3)+O(delta^3) gives the claimed width coefficient. Analytic proof covers all real parameters in the stated interval, including endpoints; the standalone code additionally checks exact finite incidence, numerical quadrature and seeded Haar simulation. No claim about the missing lower tail.

value.rationale: The recent four-dimensional isoperimetric characterization promotes the regular 24-cell as a canonical tiling body. For that object, the exact tail distribution covering about 93.6357 percent of Haar directions is a natural, non-tabulated one-dimensional projection invariant. Its first analytic transition has a sharp order-two singularity with a coefficient reflecting 96 geometrically adjacent vertex-cap pairs. This is a structurally motivated cutoff with reproducible integral-geometric content, not an arbitrary numerical slice; the lower tail and independent validation remain open.
